sections.h2: What is Bullitt County, Kentucky, like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Bullitt County is the Louisville suburb that grew into a distribution hub. It sits just south of Jefferson County, with Spencer, Nelson and Hardin counties on its other sides, and covers 300 square miles in the Knobs region of the western Bluegrass. Shepherdsville is the county seat and the oldest town. Mount Washington is the largest city, and ten miles of Kentucky 44 link the two with homes along nearly the whole stretch.

Interstate 65 runs through the middle of the county. More than six million square feet of distribution and warehouse space has been built since 2000, with business parks about 16 miles from Louisville's airport and the UPS Worldport. The western fifth of the county, about 62 square miles, belongs to Fort Knox training land. UofL Health South Hospital opened in Shepherdsville in March 2024, and Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest in Clermont is a visitor draw. The county's tourism impact was estimated at $173.2 million for 2025.

Bullitt's Lick, a salt lick near the Salt River, supplied Kentucky's first industry until around 1830, and the county was organized from parts of Jefferson and Nelson counties by an act approved December 13, 1796.

sections.h2: How do Bullitt County housing numbers compare?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population at 86,454, up 5.1 percent from 82,224 in the April 2020 base. The housing figures run higher than in nearby rural counties:

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $247,200 (2020 to 2024), the highest of Boyle, Bracken, Breckinridge and Bullitt.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 84.9 percent across 31,747 households.
  • Median gross rent: $987, and median owner cost with a mortgage $1,561 a month.
  • Median household income: $80,558, with 8.5 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 654, against 34,722 housing units.

The mean commute is 28.7 minutes. Transportation and warehousing receipts in 2022 reached $327.8 million, which fits a county where trucking and logistics employ many residents. Density is 276.8 people per square mile.

sections.h2: Which Bullitt County office collects the property tax?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Office takes the money and distributes it to the state, county, schools and special districts. Its office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville, phone 502-543-2514, and it collects over $170 million a year. Mail goes to PO Box 205, Shepherdsville, KY 40165. Between October 1 and December 31 you can also pay by check at any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county.

Assessments belong to the PVA, whose county annex office is at 149 North Walnut Street, phone 502-543-7480. The County Clerk, at 502-955-6369, gives payoff figures for delinquent bills from earlier years.

sections.h2: What are the Bullitt County tax dates?
sections.html:
The sheriff receives the bills from the clerk at the end of September and most owners see them in the first week of October. The 2026 bills list four due dates, by receipt or postmark:

  • November 1: face value less a 2 percent discount.
  • December 31: face value.
  • January 31: face value plus a 5 percent penalty.
  • April 15: face value plus a 21 percent penalty.

After April 1, the sheriff no longer accepts personal or business checks. Pay with cash, a certified check, a money order or a card. Card fees are set by the processor. Partial payments are refused, and an owner who has not received a bill by mid-October should call for a duplicate.

sections.h2: What is the Bullitt County tax rate for 2026?
sections.html:
The sheriff publishes a rate chart for each jurisdiction. The figures below are the 2026 real estate rates, which appear to follow the cents per $100 convention that the state rate uses.

2026 Bullitt County real estate rates by jurisdiction (source: Bullitt County Sheriff)
JurisdictionReal estate rate
State10.30
County8.7
Health2.4
Library4.9
School73.10
County Extension0.90
Shepherdsville10.10
Mount Washington Fire20.0

The first six lines add up to 100.30. The Nichols, Southeast and Zoneton fire districts are each 10.0, and a Plum Creek water line of 1.0 applies to real estate in its area. Shepherdsville's own tax comes combined with the county bill. Other incorporated places, including Mount Washington, Hillview, Hunters Hollow, Pioneer Village, Fox Chase, Lebanon Junction and Hebron Estates, bill their own city tax, so call the city. The tax district code on the bill tells you which applies.

sections.h2: Which Bullitt County school district applies?
sections.html: Bullitt County Public Schools serves nearly the whole county and accounts for the largest line on the bill at 73.10. The Department of Defense Education Activity runs the schools on Fort Knox, including Fort Knox Middle High School. The county's high schools are Bullitt Central in Shepherdsville, Bullitt East in Mount Washington, North Bullitt in Hebron Estates and Riverview. Bernheim, Bullitt Lick, Eastside, Hebron, Mount Washington and Zoneton run the middle schools.

sections.h2: Who gets the homestead exemption in Bullitt County?
sections.html: An owner who is 65 or older on January 1 and lives in the home can reduce the assessment by up to $49,100. The sheriff's page tells owners to bring proof of age, such as a driver's license, to the PVA with the application before paying. A totally disabled owner qualifies under the state rule as well. The application goes to the PVA by December 31 of the tax year.

sections.h2: How does an assessment appeal work in Bullitt County?
sections.html: Request a conference at the PVA once the notice arrives. The tax roll is open for inspection for thirteen days starting the first Monday in May, and a filing at the County Clerk is due the workday after the inspection period ends. The board of assessment appeals sits for as many as five days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Bring comparable sales and photos, because the board decides on evidence and a case with none is denied.

sections.h2: How should a Bullitt County seller handle the tax at closing?
sections.html: The bill goes to the January 1 owner. A house that sells in the spring is still billed to the seller, and the closing agent divides the year between the parties. The sheriff requires the full bill to be paid, so the settlement statement must show who pays. Anything unpaid after April 15 moves to the clerk with a lien, and interest runs 1 percent a month; ask for a payoff before the closing date. Sellers with inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses can often close with a cash buyer and have the tax paid from proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the Bullitt County sheriff's phone number for taxes?
faqs.a: Call 502-543-2514. The office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville.

faqs.q: When does the Bullitt County 2% discount end?
faqs.a: For the 2026 bills it ends November 1, by receipt or postmark. December 31 is face value, January 31 adds 5 percent, and April 15 adds 21 percent.

faqs.q: Can I pay Bullitt County taxes at a bank?
faqs.a: Yes. Any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county takes check payments from October 1 to December 31 during business hours.

faqs.q: Does Shepherdsville charge a separate city tax?
faqs.a: No separate bill. Shepherdsville's tax is combined with the county bill, while other cities such as Mount Washington and Hillview bill their own city tax.

faqs.q: How much is the Bullitt County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Up to $49,100 off the assessed value for owners 65 or older who live in the home on January 1. Apply at the PVA before paying the bill.
